angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 587,171 km at 82.75 pc = 0.09 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 12.0845 +/- 0.0145 mas (same row, RUWE 1.00): 82.75 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.844 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Heidari et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-5076 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...694A..36H/abstract): 587,171 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.789 +/- 0.046 solar masses from Heidari et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-5076 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...694A..36H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4780 +/- 120 K from Heidari et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5076 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...694A..36H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Heidari et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5076 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...694A..36H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-5076.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.482, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
